concepts.def: Skull, spine, ribs, sternum — central column.
Arms, legs, shoulder and pelvic girdles.
Bone longer than wide — e.g. femur, humerus.
Thin and broad — e.g. skull, sternum, ribs.
Complex shape — e.g. vertebrae of the spine.

walkthroughs.body_html: Skeleton functions: support, protection, movement, blood cell production (in bone marrow) and mineral storage (calcium, phosphorus). All five are essential for life and sport.
The axial skeleton is the central core — skull, spine, ribs, sternum. The appendicular skeleton is everything else — arms, legs and the girdles that attach them to the core.
Five bone types: long (femur, leverage), short (carpals, shock absorption), flat (skull, protection), irregular (vertebrae, mixed roles) and sesamoid (patella, embedded in tendon to reduce friction).
